correctness.rationale: Monotone DNF identifies every positive truth set with a unique upset of the realised valuation poset. On the no-duplicate matching event, the upset lattice factors as a product of three- and two-element chains. Shared-vertex comparisons are at most 4(5/8)^m, local-dependence Poisson approximation and union bounds yield a valid finite total-variation error. The exponential factors 5/(3 sqrt(3)), sqrt(3)/2 and 2/3 are below one at the critical scale. Standalone exact checks cover 5058 small valuation systems, 245 eligible lattice factorizations and six exact moment bounds; finite experiments are not treated as infinite proof.

Stark 2004 already supplies the underlying Poisson comparable-pair count; neither that result nor finite upset duality is newly claimed. value.rationale: The full bounded lattice of truth sets defines a canonical expressivity invariant for finite positive propositional models. The precise three-chain factor law at onset and the retained-definability distribution are semantically distinct from the preexisting yes/no comparability threshold or count; they determine an entire natural random finite distributive-lattice isomorphism type and quantifiable information loss. This is a complete natural invariant motivated by the comparison with Boolean definability, not a contrived finite slice.
